Per-tool parameters, generated from the registry's input schemas —

<!-- TOOL_DETAILS_START (generated by scripts/dump_tool_table.py) -->
### mail-read

#### `list_folders` — read (min tier: read)

List mail folders as a depth-limited tree walk. Each row is {id, name, path, total, unread, children}; `id` is a short folder alias (f7) reusable as a `folder`/`parent` argument anywhere. Well-known folders also carry `wk` (e.g. 'f:inbox') — prefer passing that stable alias. Rows also carry the raw EWS FolderClass as `folder_class` when Exchange reports one (e.g. 'IPF.Note' for mail, 'IPF.Appointment' for calendar). Set include_empty=false to hide folders with zero items.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parent` | string | no | Start folder: well-known alias (f:inbox), folder alias (f7), path, or raw id. Default: the message-folder root. |
| `depth` | integer | no | (default `2`) |
| `include_empty` | boolean | no | (default `True`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `search_messages` — read (min tier: read)

Search mail. TWO ENGINES, mutually exclusive: pass `query` (an Exchange AQS string, e.g. 'from:alice@example.com subject:rfp hasattachment:yes') OR the structured filters (sender/subject/since/until/is_unread/has_attachments/categories/flag_complete) — combining `query` with any structured filter is a validation error. `sender` is matched client-side against the fetched page's sender email/name, so total_available is unknown when it is used. Results are compact cards, newest first; their `id` values are short aliases (m12) for get_message / get_thread / get_attachment. If an id later goes stale (items move), re-run this search for fresh ids.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | no | AQS query string — cannot be combined with the structured filters below. |
| `folder` | string | no | Folder alias (f:inbox, f:sent, f7), path, raw id, or f:all for the whole mailbox: all mail folders with their subfolders, without deleted items, junk, drafts and outbox; each hit then names its folder. (default `f:inbox`) |
| `sender` | string | no | Sender email or display-name substring, matched within each page; keep paging while next_offset is set (a page may hold fewer than `limit` items or none, and total_available is null on live searches). |
| `from_` | string | no | DEPRECATED alias of `sender` — do not combine the two. |
| `subject` | string | no | Subject substring. |
| `since` | string | no | Window start: 'today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime (server timezone). |
| `until` | string | no | Window end: 'today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime (server timezone). |
| `is_unread` | boolean | no |  |
| `has_attachments` | boolean | no |  |
| `categories` | array | no | Match messages carrying all listed Outlook categories; live search uses contains matching whereas the local mirror matches exact category elements. Cannot combine with `query`. |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | Search `folder` and all mail folders under it, merged newest first; each card carries `folder` and the result reports `folders_searched`. Always runs live. (default `False`) |
| `flag_complete` | boolean | no | true matches messages whose follow-up flag is marked Complete; false matches all other messages (unflagged or still-open flag). Always runs live and cannot combine with `query`. |
| `offset` | integer | no | (default `0`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `20`) |
| `mode` | string | no | semantic = hybrid FTS + vector retrieval (only when the semantic tier is enabled; requires `query`; other filters ignored). (one of: `keyword`, `semantic`; default `keyword`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `check_messages` — read (min tier: read)

Check a whole list of values against one mail folder in one call: which values occur as a whole word in a message subject (or in the sender name/address) and which are missing. Returns up to 5 matching cards per value. Use this instead of one search_messages call per value.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | string/array | yes | Values separated by commas or new lines, or an array of strings (a JSON array string is accepted too). At most 200. |
| `field` | string | no | Where to look for each value (default subject). (one of: `subject`, `sender`) |
| `folder` | string | no | Single mail folder alias, path, or raw id, e.g. f:inbox (default) or f:sent (f:all and recursive scopes are not supported). |
| `since` | string | no | Received at or after (ISO date). |
| `until` | string | no | Received at or before (ISO date). |
| `only_missing` | boolean | no | Return only the values without a match. |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_message` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch one message by id (short alias from search results, e.g. m12; raw EWS ids also work). format='full' (default) returns recipients, the cleaned body (quoted history stripped — use get_thread for the conversation) and the attachment inventory; format='concise' returns the compact card. `flag_complete` is only reported when read live, i.e. with fresh=true. A not_found means the id went stale (items move) — re-run search_messages and retry with a fresh id.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Message id (m-alias or raw). |
| `format` | string | no | (one of: `full`, `concise`; default `full`) |
| `include_html` | boolean | no | Also return the raw HTML body (rendering edge cases only — it is token-expensive). (default `False`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_thread` — read (min tier: read)

Rebuild the conversation containing the given message id: Inbox and Sent are merged and sorted chronologically, each entry's body cleaned to its latest-reply-only text. Returns thread_id (t-alias), participants with message counts, and the most recent `limit` entries. Entry ids are m-aliases usable with get_message/get_attachment. Stale id → re-run search_messages.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Any message id in the thread (m-alias or raw). |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `20`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | History paging: 0 = the most recent entries; pass the returned next_offset for older ones. (default `0`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_attachment` — read (min tier: read)

Read one attachment of a message. mode='info' → metadata only; 'text' → decoded UTF-8 text (capped at 20000 chars, `truncated` flagged) for text-like attachments (text/* content type or .txt/.csv/.md/.log/.json name); 'save' → write the bytes under the server data dir and return saved_path; 'auto' (default) → text when text-like, otherwise info plus a hint. An smime.p7m attachment (application/pkcs7-mime) is sniffed and reported as `smime_type: signed|enveloped` — signed is NOT encrypted (auto decodes as text, cert/signature bytes show as replacement chars); enveloped IS encrypted (auto stays info; content is unrecoverable without the recipient's private key). When the message has several attachments you MUST pick one via `attachment` (a name, or a zero-based index as a string).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message_id` | string | yes | Message id (m-alias or raw). |
| `attachment` | string | no | Attachment name or zero-based index as a string (e.g. '0'). Optional only when the message has exactly one attachment. |
| `mode` | string | no | (one of: `auto`, `info`, `text`, `save`; default `auto`) |

#### `get_mailbox_overview` — read (min tier: read)

The morning-brief workflow tool — start here. One call returns unread_total, the 10 most recent unread message cards, today's calendar events (recurrences expanded) across `horizon_days` days, and the Exchange connection state. Card ids are short aliases (m12 / e3) for the other tools.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `horizon_days` | integer | no | (default `1`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

### calendar / people / status

#### `list_events` — read (min tier: read)

List calendar events overlapping a time window (default: today through +7d, server timezone). Recurring meetings are expanded into individual occurrences — a weekly meeting shows once per occurrence in the window. Returns a paged envelope of compact event cards; their ids are short aliases (e1, e2, …) you pass to get_event.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | string | no | Window start: 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. (default `today`) |
| `end` | string | no | Window end (exclusive): 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. (default `+7d`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | Pagination offset into the window. (default `0`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Max events returned. (default `25`) |

#### `get_event` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch one calendar event in full by id (a short alias like 'e3' from list_events, or a raw EWS id). Returns organizer, every attendee with their response (Accept/Decline/Tentative/…), the cleaned body text, a recurring flag, the rule of a series, the reminder (null if none), your own response and, for an event you organize, whether invitations were sent.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Event id — alias (e1, e2, …) or raw EWS id. |

#### `check_availability` — read (min tier: read)

Check free/busy for one or more attendees and propose meeting slots. Each returned slot is a candidate start/end (30-minute grid) of duration_minutes where EVERY listed attendee is free; per_attendee shows the raw busy blocks behind the answer. With working_hours_only (default true) slots are confined to 09:00-17:00 in the server timezone. An empty slots list means no common free window exists in the range.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attendees` | array | yes | SMTP email addresses to check. |
| `start` | string | yes | Window start: 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. |
| `end` | string | yes | Window end: 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. |
| `duration_minutes` | integer | no | Desired meeting length. (default `30`) |
| `working_hours_only` | boolean | no | Confine slots to 09:00-17:00. (default `True`) |

#### `find_people` — read (min tier: read)

Find people by name or email fragment in the GAL (global address list) and/or the personal contacts folder. source='auto' merges both, deduplicating by email with the GAL entry winning. Returned ids are short aliases (p1, p2, …).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Name or email fragment, e.g. 'alice@example.com'. |
| `source` | string | no | Where to search; auto = GAL + contacts. (one of: `auto`, `gal`, `contacts`; default `auto`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Max people returned. (default `10`) |

#### `get_contact` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch one person in full by id — a p-alias from find_people, a raw contact id, or a plain email address. Returns name/email/title/company/phone where known, plus mirror-derived history (first/last contact, sent/received counts) when the local mirror is warm.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | p-alias, raw contact id, or email. |

#### `get_oof_settings` — read (min tier: read)

Read the mailbox out-of-office (automatic reply) settings: state (disabled/enabled/scheduled), the scheduled window when applicable, and the internal/external reply texts (HTML stripped, capped at 500 chars).

_No parameters._

#### `get_server_status` — read (min tier: read)

This server's own status: version, uptime, Exchange connection state, capability tier, send kill-switch, tool count, per-tool call counters and alias statistics. Never touches Exchange — it answers even while the connection is still warming up, so use it to explain connectivity problems.

_No parameters._

### tasks / waiting-on

#### `list_tasks` — read (min tier: read)

List Exchange tasks (to-dos), incomplete ones by default. Returns {id, subject, due, complete, status}; ids are short aliases (k1, k2, …) for update_task. Served from the local mirror when synced (source=cache), live otherwise.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_completed` | boolean | no | (default `False`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | (default `0`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `25`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read. (default `False`) |

#### `update_task` — write (min tier: draft)

Update ONE task: mark it complete and/or set its due date ('today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD). Nothing else is editable here — task planning belongs to the calling assistant, not the server.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Task id (k-alias from list_tasks or raw). |
| `complete` | boolean | no |  |
| `due` | string | no | New due date: 'today', '+Nd', or YYYY-MM-DD. |

#### `waiting_on` — read (min tier: read)

Deterministic mirror query: messages YOU sent whose thread has received no inbound reply after `days` days — the 'what am I waiting on?' list. Each row carries the sent message id, the thread alias, recipients and a snippet. Requires the local mirror (sent folder synced).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | no | (default `5`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `25`) |

### writes

#### `create_draft` — write (min tier: draft)

Author mail as a DRAFT (never sends). mode=new needs to+body; reply/reply_all/forward need reply_to (the original message id) and quote the original server-side; forward also needs to. body is plain text (the server wraps it in minimal HTML). importance applies to mode=new only. attachments adds files; if one fails the draft still exists and attachments_failed names it. Use send_draft to send.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | no | (one of: `new`, `reply`, `reply_all`, `forward`; default `new`) |
| `reply_to` | string | no |  |
| `to` | array | no |  |
| `cc` | array | no |  |
| `bcc` | array | no |  |
| `subject` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | yes |  |
| `importance` | string | no | (one of: `normal`, `high`) |
| `attachments` | array | no |  |

#### `update_draft` — write (min tier: draft)

Update fields of an existing draft (to/cc/bcc/subject/body). Only the supplied fields change.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |
| `to` | array | no |  |
| `cc` | array | no |  |
| `bcc` | array | no |  |
| `subject` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | no |  |

#### `add_draft_attachment` — write (min tier: draft)

Add one file to an existing draft (via content_base64 or path inside EWS_ATTACHMENT_DIR). Refuses items that are not in f:drafts. Returns all attachments of the draft.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |
| `filename` | string | no | File name; required with content_base64, defaults to the file's own name when path is given. |
| `content_base64` | string | no | The file content, base64-encoded (mutually exclusive with path). |
| `path` | string | no | Relative file path inside EWS_ATTACHMENT_DIR (mutually exclusive with content_base64). |
| `content_type` | string | no | MIME type; derived from the file name if omitted. |

#### `delete_draft` — write (min tier: draft)

Move a draft to trash (recoverable). Refuses items that are not in f:drafts.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |

#### `update_messages` — write (min tier: draft)

Bulk-update up to 50 messages: set_read, categories_add/categories_remove, and/or flag_complete. Per-item failures are isolated and reported. flag_complete marks/unmarks the message's follow-up flag as Complete (true) or clears completion (false) - it does not raise a NEW follow-up flag on an unflagged message, only sets/clears the completion state.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes |  |
| `set_read` | boolean | no |  |
| `categories_add` | array | no |  |
| `categories_remove` | array | no |  |
| `flag_complete` | boolean | no |  |

#### `move_messages` — write (min tier: draft)

Move up to 50 messages to a folder (id, f:alias or path). Message ids are re-bound automatically: the SAME id keeps working after the move.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes |  |
| `to_folder` | string | yes |  |

#### `create_event` — write (min tier: draft)

Create a calendar event or, with recurrence, a recurring series. Default send_invitations=false saves it like a draft WITHOUT emailing attendees (no confirm needed): they stay on the event, and the organizer can send it from Outlook. With send_invitations=true, invitations leave the org: two-phase confirm + send kill-switch apply. Without reminder_minutes the event has no reminder.

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subject` | string | yes |  |
| `start` | string | yes |  |
| `end` | string | yes |  |
| `attendees` | array | no |  |
| `location` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | no |  |
| `reminder_minutes` | integer | no | Remind this many minutes before the start; 0 is at the start. |
| `recurrence` | object | no | Repeat the event. start and end are the first occurrence; the time of day stays the same across DST changes. Without until or count the series has no end. |
| `send_invitations` | boolean | no | (default `False`) |

#### `update_event` — write (min tier: draft)

Update event fields (subject/start/end/location/body/reminder). An occurrence id from list_events changes that occurrence only; scope='series' changes the whole series and overwrites those fields on occurrences changed individually before. Default notify_attendees=false is a silent metadata edit; true notifies changed attendees → two-phase confirm + send kill-switch apply.

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | yes |  |
| `subject` | string | no |  |
| `start` | string | no |  |
| `end` | string | no |  |
| `location` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | no |  |
| `reminder_minutes` | integer | no | Remind this many minutes before the start; 0 is at the start, -1 removes the reminder. |
| `scope` | string | no | For recurring events. With 'series', start and end must be on the series' first date. (one of: `occurrence`, `series`) |
| `notify_attendees` | boolean | no | (default `False`) |

#### `send_draft` — send (min tier: full)

Send an existing draft (the ONLY way mail leaves this mailbox). Two-phase: the first call fetches the draft and returns its REAL recipients/subject/body/attachments as a preview + confirm_token bound to that content; the second call with the token re-verifies the content and sends (editing the draft in between invalidates the token). Optional idempotency_key dedupes retries (replays return the stored result).

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |
| `idempotency_key` | string | no |  |

#### `respond_to_event` — send (min tier: full)

Accept/tentative/decline a meeting — this SENDS a response to the organizer, so it is two-phase confirmed.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | yes |  |
| `response` | string | yes | (one of: `accept`, `decline`, `tentative`) |
| `message` | string | no |  |

#### `cancel_event` — destructive (min tier: full)

Cancel a meeting you organize — sends cancellations to all attendees (destructive, two-phase confirmed).

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | yes |  |
| `message` | string | no |  |

#### `delete_messages` — destructive (min tier: full)

Delete up to 50 messages. disposition: 'trash' (default, recoverable), 'soft' (dumpster) or 'permanent' (UNRECOVERABLE — requires two-phase confirm). Class is destructive, so ALL dispositions need the full tier in v5.0 (conservative).

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes |  |
| `disposition` | string | no | (one of: `trash`, `soft`, `permanent`; default `trash`) |

#### `set_oof` — send (min tier: full)

Set out-of-office auto-replies (externally visible → send class, two-phase confirmed). state: disabled|enabled|scheduled; scheduled needs start+end. external_reply defaults to internal_reply when omitted.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string | yes | (one of: `disabled`, `enabled`, `scheduled`) |
| `internal_reply` | string | no |  |
| `external_reply` | string | no |  |
| `start` | string | no |  |
| `end` | string | no |  |

### inbox rules

#### `list_rules` — read (min tier: read)

List server-side Exchange Inbox rules. Reports every rule with an r-alias id, conditions, actions, and editable=true|false (plus unsupported fields, sends_mail/recipients for rules that send or forward mail, and in_error when Exchange flagged the rule). Top-level outlook_only_rules (true|false|null) indicates whether Outlook-only client rules exist that any EWS rule write would remove.

_No parameters._

#### `save_rule` — write (min tier: draft)

Create a server-side Inbox rule or wholesale-replace an existing editable rule (pass rule_id to replace). Only mailbox-internal actions are allowed (move_to_folder, copy_to_folder, assign_categories, mark_as_read, mark_importance, stop_processing_rules); sending/forwarding/deleting actions are refused, and rules with editable=false cannot be replaced. Always two-phase confirmed; warns when conditions are empty or Outlook-only rules would be lost.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `actions` | object | yes | Mailbox-internal rule actions (at least one must be enabled). Sending, forwarding, redirecting, server replies, and deleting are never writable. |
| `conditions` | object | no | Predicates an incoming message must match. Omitting conditions or passing {} matches every incoming message (warned in preview). |
| `priority` | integer | no | Execution order (1 runs first). (default `1`) |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | (default `True`) |
| `rule_id` | string | no | Existing r-alias to wholesale-replace; omit to create. |

#### `delete_rule` — write (min tier: draft)

Delete a server-side Inbox rule by rule_id (including rules reported with editable=false). Always two-phase confirmed; warns when Outlook-only rules exist on the mailbox.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | string | yes |  |

### semantic (only when EWS_SEMANTIC_INDEX != none)

#### `find_similar` — read (min tier: read)

Find messages semantically similar to a given one (vector similarity over cleaned bodies; Arabic + English). Returns compact cards with a `similarity` score. Only available when the optional semantic tier is enabled.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Message id (m-alias or raw) to compare against. |
| `top_k` | integer | no | (default `5`) |
<!-- TOOL_DETAILS_END -->

## The canonical envelope

Every list-shaped tool ships exactly:

```json
{"ok": true, "items": [...], "count": 3, "total_available": 120,
 "next_offset": 3, "source": "cache", "as_of": "2026-07-11T04:00:00+00:00"}
```

- `count` = `len(items)`; `total_available` is exact when cheap (local
  mirror `COUNT(*)`, a refreshed folder count on unfiltered live
  listings, or live single-folder `categories` / `flag_complete=true`
  queries without `query` or `sender`) and `null` otherwise. In
  particular, `total_available` is `null` on live
  `search_messages(flag_complete=false)` (counting uncompleted items
  would walk nearly the whole folder) and on multi-folder
  `search_messages` (`folder="f:all"` or `recursive=true`) whenever any
  folder has matches past `offset + limit`, any folder fails
  (`folders_failed`), folders exceed the 200-folder cap
  (`folders_skipped`), or `sender` is set. `next_offset` is `null` when
  no further page exists (live paths prove it with a one-item lookahead,
  never a `count()` scan).
- `source` is `cache` (with `as_of`) or `live`; pass `fresh: true` to any
  cache-first tool to force a live read.

## Ids

All ids in outputs are short aliases: `m` message, `d` draft, `e` event,
`t` thread, `p` person, `k` task, `f` folder, `r` rule. Inputs accept aliases or
raw EWS ids. A stale alias returns `not_found` with a re-search hint —
ids change when items move; re-run the search or `list_rules` for fresh ones.

## Error taxonomy

| code | HTTP | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `validation` | 400 | bad arguments (schema-checked on the REST shim) |
| `auth_failed` | 401 | missing/invalid `MCP_API_KEY`, Exchange rejected credentials (HTTP 401), or the lockout guard (`AuthBreaker`) is open (retrying will not help) |
| `tier_blocked` | 403 | tool needs a higher `EWS_CAPABILITY_TIER` |
| `kill_switch` | 403 | send-class call while `SEND_ENABLED=false` |
| `recipient_blocked` | 403 | recipient failed the allow/denylist |
| `not_found` | 404 | stale/unknown id (hint: re-search) |
| `confirm_invalid` | 409 | confirm token expired / consumed / content changed |
| `throttled` | 429 | Exchange back-off (`retry_after_s` included) |
| `rate_capped` | 429 | send rate cap reached (`retry_after_s` included) |
| `internal` | 500 | unexpected internal server error |
| `upstream_error` | 502 | Exchange failed the call |
| `upstream_unavailable` | 503 | connection cold/circuit open (`retry_after_s`) |

## Two-phase confirmation

Irreversible or standing-order tools (`send_draft`, `respond_to_event`,
`cancel_event`, `set_oof`, `save_rule`, `delete_rule`, `delete_messages`
with `disposition=permanent`, event tools when they would notify
attendees) run in two phases:

1. Call WITHOUT `confirm_token` → a preview + a short-lived token.
   Nothing executes. For `send_draft` the preview shows the draft's REAL
   `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body_snippet`, `attachment_count`, and
   `attachments`, and the token is HMAC-bound to subject, sorted
   recipients, body, and attachments (ids, names, and sizes).
2. Call again with identical arguments plus `confirm_token` → executes
   once. For `send_draft`, phase 2 fetches the draft once under the
   per-draft lock, re-checks its content hash against the verified hash,
   and sends that same object; a draft (or attachment list) changed
   after the preview is refused with `confirm_invalid`. Tokens also die
   on argument changes, on TTL expiry (`CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS`, default
   600 s), and after one use. `send_draft` retries with the same
   `idempotency_key` replay the cached receipt instead of sending twice.

## Cache freshness contract

Reads served by the local mirror carry `source: "cache"` and `as_of`
(the folder's last sync watermark; delta cadence
`EWS_CACHE_SYNC_SECONDS`, default 45 s). `fresh: true` forces live.
`get_server_status.cache` exposes per-folder watermarks, row counts, DB
size and sync health. `mode: "semantic"` on `search_messages` (and the
`find_similar` tool) exist only when `EWS_SEMANTIC_INDEX` is enabled.

## Searching several folders

`search_messages` supports two live multi-folder modes (`source: "live"`):

- `folder="f:all"` searches every `IPF.Note*` mail folder in the mailbox
  except Deleted Items (`f:trash` / `f:deleteditems`), Junk (`f:junk` /
  `f:junkemail`), Drafts (`f:drafts`), Outbox (`f:outbox`), and their
  subfolders.
- `recursive=true` searches the target `folder` and all `IPF.Note*`
  subfolders beneath it. When `folder` explicitly names Deleted Items,
  Junk, Drafts, or Outbox with `recursive=true`, that subtree is walked.

Each folder in scope is queried for up to `offset + limit` items and
merged newest first (`datetime_received` descending). Multi-folder calls
are bounded to at most `200` folders per call and `offset + limit <= 500`
(exceeding `500` fails with `validation`). If Exchange throttles any
folder, the call fails with `throttled`.

Every returned message card includes `folder` (its folder path), and the
envelope adds `folders_searched`, plus `folders_failed` (paths of
folders that failed, when non-empty) and `folders_skipped` (folders past
the `200`-folder cap, when non-zero). `sender` is matched within each
merged `offset..offset + limit` page, so a page can contain fewer than
`limit` items (or zero) while older matches remain; keep paging while
`next_offset` is non-null.

## Inbox rules

Three tools manage Exchange's server-side Inbox rules (`list_rules` at
`read`; `save_rule` and `delete_rule` at `draft`, both always two-phase
confirmed):

- **Safety contract (mailbox-internal only).** `save_rule` builds `Actions`
  strictly from six allow-listed fields: `move_to_folder`, `copy_to_folder`,
  `assign_categories`, `mark_as_read`, `mark_importance`, and
  `stop_processing_rules`. Actions that send, forward, redirect, auto-reply,
  send SMS alerts, or delete mail are never writable. `move_to_folder` and
  `copy_to_folder` refuse Deleted Items, Junk Email and any folder below
  them: filing every match there is a deleting rule under another name.
- **Read-only reporting for complex rules.** `list_rules` returns every rule
  with an `r`-alias id. Any rule that uses a non-writable action, an
  exception, a condition outside the writable set (`from_addresses`,
  `sent_to_addresses`, `subject_contains`, `body_contains`,
  `subject_or_body_contains`, `sender_contains`, `recipient_contains`,
  `has_attachments`, `importance`, `sent_to_me`, `sent_cc_me`,
  `sent_only_to_me`, `sent_to_or_cc_me`, `not_sent_to_me`), or
  `is_not_supported` is reported with `editable: false` and the field names in
  `unsupported` (plus `sends_mail: true` and `recipients` when it sends or
  forwards mail, and `in_error: true` when Exchange flags a broken rule).
  `save_rule` refuses to replace any rule with `editable: false` so
  unsupported fields are never silently dropped; `delete_rule` may delete any
  rule.
- **Outlook rule-blob caveat.** Modifying or deleting rules via EWS
  `UpdateInboxRules` sends `RemoveOutlookRuleBlob=true`, which deletes
  client-side send rules and can cause rules disabled via the Outlook UI to be
  lost. `list_rules` reads `OutlookRuleBlobExists` from Exchange and reports
  top-level `outlook_only_rules` (`true|false|null`). Both `save_rule` and
  `delete_rule` surface an explicit warning in their phase-1 preview whenever
  `outlook_only_rules` is `true` or `null` (and `save_rule` also warns when a
  rule has no conditions and therefore matches every incoming message).

## Intentionally dropped vs v3

Removed deliberately — most belong to the calling assistant (skills), not
a data-plane server:

- **One-shot send tools** (`send_email`, `reply_email`, `forward_email`):
  the ONLY way mail leaves the mailbox is `create_draft` → `send_draft`.
- **Impersonation / delegated mailboxes** (`target_mailbox` everywhere):
  one server = one mailbox.
- **OAuth2/MSAL flows**: the target deployment is on-prem Exchange with
  auto-negotiated auth; a Graph/OAuth backend would be a different
  gateway, not a flag.
- **Contacts folder management** (create/update/delete contacts).
- **Folder management** (create/rename/delete folders).
- **MIME export** and raw-content endpoints.
- **The agent-secretary stack** (server-side classify/summarize/brief/
  voice/commitments/approval queue): the caller already IS an LLM;
  `examples/skills/exchange-assistant/` shows the skill-side pattern.
